verdict.persistent_destination: One DWORD in the singleton lifetime manager pointer-slot vector.
verdict.second_array_publication_explanation: For the attributed getter call, the registration/entry-storage code treats GlobalConfig as a DWORD value. Destinations are lifetime manager vector storage, manager header fields or invocation/iterator-result stack words; no destination is derived from the GlobalConfig owner value.
verdict.qualification: This closes the direct registration-store classification, not the complete escaped-owner graph. Current CRT handlers/decoder services, allocator/exception internals, future consumers and eventual current-method-table scalar deletion remain open. Malformed vector pointers aliasing arbitrary memory are not proved impossible.

identities.G: Native GlobalConfig owner returned/published by 00432650; allocation size 0x2E8.
identities.M: Native singleton lifetime manager returned by 00415350. Distinct from G.

manager_layout.plus_10: section pointer used by getter, untouched by registration entries

getter_escape.abi: 00432650 consumes no input and returns published owner in EAX, plain RET.
getter_escape.publication: 004326D4 writes the constructor result G (or zero) to 00F878E4 before registration.
getter_escape.lock_boundary: Getter captures the first manager section at +0x10, enters it and increments section+0x18 before rechecking/constructing. After normal registration it decrements that captured section counter and leaves. BD0C30 and its vector wrappers add no internal lock.
getter_escape.limits: Constructor effects, manager construction, OS section internals and getter exceptional unwind were not re-audited. The captured G pointer publication precedes error-handler or allocator callbacks reached by registration.

core_contracts.name: register
core_contracts.abi: ECX=M, stack object DWORD G; RET 4.
behavior: Capture current M+8 and compare unsigned M+4 <= end. On failure call 00BF6713 and continue if it returns.
Only after validation, test the current object stack argument for zero. Null skips append.
For non-null, pass the address of that actual object argument word to 00BD0BC0.
core_contracts.stores: No non-stack store in this body. It does not read [G] or any field of G.

core_contracts.name: append
core_contracts.abi: ECX=M, stack pointer to value word; RET 4.
behavior: Capture M+4; compute raw modulo32 size/capacity using subtraction then SAR 2.
A non-null begin with unsigned size below capacity uses the direct path: capture M+8, load *value_slot, store it at the captured end, then publish captured end+4 to M+8.
Otherwise capture end, validate captured begin <= captured end, then call 00BD08D0 with an eight-byte local result buffer, iterator owner M, captured position=end and the current value-slot argument.

stores.value: G loaded from registration stack word

core_contracts.name: checked_insert_one
core_contracts.abi: ECX=M; stack result, iterator_owner, position, value_slot; EAX=result; RET 0x10.
behavior: Capture begin and derive index zero for null/empty begin; otherwise validate begin/end and non-null same iterator owner, then derive (position-begin) SAR 2.
00BD0920 calls 00BD0700 using original M, passed iterator owner/position, literal count 1 and value-slot pointer.
After insertion capture current begin; validate begin/end, derive result position using saved index, validate resulting range. Returning validators continue with the native captures/reloads.
Write result.position at result+4 before result.owner at result+0. In the actual append caller this result is stack storage.

core_contracts.name: insert_count
core_contracts.abi: ECX=M; stack iterator_owner, position, count, value_slot; RET 0x10. Incoming iterator_owner word is not loaded by this body.
core_contracts.registered_owner_capture: 00BD0708 loads the DWORD through value_slot; 00BD070A replaces its own value-slot argument word with that captured value before count test and before allocation/copy/free. At this call value_slot points to registration stack storage, not to G itself.
growth: Check count against 0x3FFFFFFF - current size and call length throw 00BD0590 on failure. For registration count is exactly 1.
Grow capacity to max(size+count, capacity+capacity/2), with the native limit-overflow candidate reset to zero.
Allocate raw slots through 00BCFEB0; copy prefix through 00BD0500; fill count copies from captured value through 00BD0560; copy suffix through 00BD0500.
Reload current begin/end to derive current count, then free current non-null begin through 00BF65AC.
Publish replacement begin, capacity_end, end at 00BD080C/00BD0811/00BD0814, in that order.
in_place: Tail shorter than count: copy tail to position+count*4, fill excess at current end, advance M.end and assign insertion range.
Tail at least count: copy last count slots to old end, publish returned end, shift middle backward, assign insertion range.
Both native branches are retained in this audit; no callback or malformed-state assumptions are used to erase a branch.

stores.value: current end plus insertion byte count

core_contracts.exception_boundary: No local FS registration or replacement-buffer cleanup is added by BD0700. Allocation/copy/failure providers are explicit boundaries; getter unwind is outside this packet.

entry_storage_leaves.effect: Raw (last-first) SAR2 then *4; only zero skips 00BF67A7. Copy addresses are vector storage. Captured return destination is retained; service status ignored.
Reload *value_slot for each DWORD store at 00BD0579. For the registration invocation the pointer value came from BD0700 stack capture; the value is not dereferenced as an object.
Until address equality, reload *value_slot and store at current destination at 00BD0173, advancing 4. Destinations are vector slot ranges supplied by insertion.
Derive raw destination begin; signed-positive count calls 00BF67A7, service status ignored. Copies vector bytes only under the attributed provenance.

callbacks_and_services.dispatch: BF66EF reads 0109DD64, passes it to 00C04FDE, and if result is non-null tail-jumps EAX at 00BF6703. Otherwise it calls 00C04EF3 with 2 then jumps 00BF65BB.
callbacks_and_services.boundary: Handler may return. Its current identity, body, and side effects are not established. No registered-owner pointer is explicitly supplied as an argument.

callbacks_and_services.native_arguments: destination, destination_bytes, source, count_bytes from vector copy leaves
callbacks_and_services.dispatch: Count zero returns success. Null destination/source or too-small destination writes errno through 00BFFB8B and calls 00BF66EF with five zero words. The valid branch calls 00BF87E0 memmove.
callbacks_and_services.boundary: Underlying memmove, errno provider and current invalid handler are not expanded. Caller ignores status; no silent early-exit repair is inferred.

callbacks_and_services.native_arguments: BCFEB0 receives count in ECX and allocates count*4 after unsigned overflow check; operator_new receives byte size.
callbacks_and_services.dispatch: BF681B calls BF9F1A malloc; on failure C055B1 rereads 0109DE44, obtains a current pointer through 00C04FDE and calls it at 00C055C5 with the byte size. A nonzero result retries allocation.
callbacks_and_services.boundary: Original malloc/heap/free internals and any additional heap/newmode handlers remain outside. The failure branch constructs/throws library bad_alloc through BF6885; current handler and exception effects are open.

callbacks_and_services.native_arguments: encoded/current pointer argument from handler dispatchers
callbacks_and_services.dispatch: Reads current TLS/IAT/PTD state or Win32 module path, obtains a decoder callback, optionally calls it with the argument, writes that result back to its own stack argument, then reloads it.
callbacks_and_services.boundary: Those current service identities and service side effects are not resolved by this packet. Decoding is not treated as a pure identity operation.

callbacks_and_services.dispatch: Builds a temporary legacy string from literal 00CE37E0 using 00408720, constructs a local exception payload through 00411700, installs 00D69260 and calls BF6885 with metadata 00D83F98.
callbacks_and_services.boundary: Existing canonical allocation/throw review covers its implementation. String/exception/runtime provider closure and caller unwind effects are not reconstructed again here.
It is a real CRT free dependency, not a no-op; no G pointer is passed by BD0700 on the attributed vector path.

lifecycle_boundaries.registration: Stores one exact object pointer for later manager consumption, with no per-owner entry constructor, callback record, type check, duplicate suppression or AddRef.
lifecycle_boundaries.normal_fast_path: With a valid manager vector and available capacity, registration performs no registered-owner method call or CRT validation/allocation callback.
lifecycle_boundaries.error_and_growth_paths: Service callbacks may run, and returning handlers continue. G was already published in 00F878E4, so possible external service reentry or side effects cannot be excluded merely because G is not an explicit callback argument.
lifecycle_boundaries.future_owner_use: Eventual lifetime-manager draining, current owner method-table lookup and terminal scalar-deletion behavior are explicitly outside the inspected registration contract. Existing lifecycle/source reviews describe that separate consumer boundary; they are not promoted to GlobalConfig terminal-path proof.
not_established: No whole-program writers through other escapes
Original CRT/FH3/SEH closure or native binary compatibility

facts: src/global_config.cpp publishes context.singleton_00f878e4 then obtains a second manager and calls its register_object interface.
The typed ConcreteSingletonLifetimeManager contains the register/append implementation and a distinct required destroy_registered callback.
Complete raw vector registration wrappers, insertion, leaf and allocation source modules already exist with dedicated prior audits. No duplicate implementation or new test is added.
These source observations are separate from native pointer provenance and do not resolve a current executable terminal deletion profile or bind every source provider.

validation.validation_limits: Full byte/linear decode preservation includes return, tail-jump and final throw-call entries; it is not transitive service closure or execution.
